requirements.statement: Every active accepted requirement SHALL have exactly one canonical Conformance correspondence declaring applicability mechanical or none.
Every mechanically applicable requirement SHALL resolve through its canonical correspondence to at least one executable assertion with stable assertion identity.
FS0 Conformance SHALL use assertion, support, evidence, and orchestration as its only required top-level primitive roles.
Assertion identity SHALL remain distinct from implementation-callable identity; multiple assertions MAY share implementation only when assertion identity and provenance remain distinct.
Every maintained Conformance primitive SHALL resolve to accepted normative authority.
Every executable assertion SHALL produce or resolve the evidence required by FS0 Conformance authority.
Every gating assertion SHALL be reachable from authorized canonical Conformance execution.
FS0 Conformance evidence SHALL be sufficient to demonstrate that conforming state is accepted, targeted violating state is rejected, and required assertions actually execute.
FS0 SHALL provide one canonical remotely runnable Conformance surface through GitHub Actions, with repo/conformance/run.py as the canonical repository execution entry point invoked by the workflow.

Before cutover, execution of candidate Conformance machinery SHALL be bootstrap mechanical verification evidence only; after cutover the accepted execution surface SHALL become canonical FS0 Conformance unless later changed through Governance.

Each installed Conformance correspondence record SHALL contain requirement_id, applicability, and assertion_ids; applicability mechanical SHALL require at least one stable assertion identity and applicability none SHALL require an empty assertion_ids collection.

In the fixed FS0 GitHub binding, canonical Conformance execution SHALL use the repository GitHub Actions workflow and Conformance evidence SHALL be a workflow or check result tied to the exact candidate commit SHA.
